🚨 NGINX2ROOT FOLLOW-UP: FIVE NGINX RCE PATHS, PLUS A CHAIN TO HOST ROOT  Follow-up to our earlier NGINX2Root post: Xint's full write-up is out, and it adds detail beyond CVE-2026-123007.  What's new: • Five independent flaws, each a separate attack path depending on configuration: CVE-2026-123007 (HTTP/2), CVE-2026-123633 (HTTP/2 with an upstream), CVE-2026-121810 (HTTP/3 with an upstream), CVE-2026-123634 (resolver, request-derived proxy_pass and mirror) and CVE-2026-113425 (mail proxy with auth_http) • Disabling HTTP/2 blocks only two of the five, so it is not a full workaround • Xint chained an nginx worker RCE with a Linux kernel SCTP flaw to get root on the host, including out of a Docker container. Xint is withholding kernel exploit details until a patch exists, and says hosts that don't use SCTP can block the module from loading • Xint says its exploit worked on AWS, GCP and Azure targets, including over a public HTTPS endpoint • Exposure: per Xint's Shodan check on Nov 10, 98.9% of nginx hosts reporting a version fall in the CVE-2026-123007 range (1.9.5-1.31.8). Version strings can be misleading, and distro packages may carry backported fixes  Fix: NGINX Open Source 1.30.7 (stable) or 1.31.9 (mainline). Restart nginx or do a live binary upgrade, because a config reload alone does not replace the running executable.  ⚠️ Analyst Note: The nginx flaws give code execution as the worker account, not root by themselves. The root step needs the separate kernel bug. We have seen no report of exploitation in the wild so far, but multiple teams have working exploits, so prioritize internet-facing nginx.  nginx2root.com/ #DDW #NGINX #nginx2root #CVE2026123007 #RCE #ThreatIntelligence #CyberSecurity

Another simple explanation is that an average software update has a low to medium chance of breaking the system. Previously, orgs navigated this by performing extensive testing, then rolling out updates a few systems at a time.  With the severity of some of these security issues being fixed, they can't afford to wait that long. The options are: risk breaking something by rolling out updates too fast, or get hacked and risk lots of things getting broken.  Given that we just had a major vulnerability in PHP, and many organizations run PHP, it's not unexpected that we would see some major companies having software outages. PHP applications are highly version specific. Attempting to update PHP is a very well known cause of software breaking.  Now, combine that with the fact that many orgs are running with less than the minimum viable number of employees. They got overexcited about AI and tripped over their own feet rushing to preemptively lay off double digit percentages of their workforce.  I'm not surprised that there's a ridiculous number of major outages. I'm surprised that there aren't far more. It's amazing some of these companies have managed to hold it together as long as they have. But expect it to only get worse from here on.

Researchers found that attackers could exploit case-insensitive public key matching to gain unauthorized access, with specially crafted keys taking less than a minute to generate. Additional vulnerabilities could allow unverified email addresses to be used for account impersonation through external services, expose restricted repository information, and bypass API token access restrictions. Security updates are available in Forgejo 17.0.2 and 15.0.12 LTS. Administrators are urged to upgrade. 🚨 New attack bypasses Windows Hello and BitLocker security, cracking PINs in hours instead of months Security researchers at TU Berlin have demonstrated a hardware attack dubbed "Hello Again" that bypasses TPM lockout protections, allowing attackers with physical access to repeatedly guess Windows Hello and BitLocker PINs. The attack manipulates security counters stored in motherboard flash memory, reducing the estimated worst-case time to crack a 4-digit Windows Hello PIN from 69 days to just 40 hours. A 6-digit BitLocker PIN could be cracked in approximately 20 days instead of 19 years. The vulnerabilities affect certain AMD and Intel-based systems. AMD has acknowledged one flaw as CVE-2026-43613 and is preparing firmware updates. Researchers recommend longer PINs to reduce the risk. Source: https:// arxiv.org/abs/2611.18126

Researchers demonstrated how it could be chained with a separate Linux kernel vulnerability to gain full root access, even escaping Docker containers. According to Xint, approximately 11.8 million servers run NGINX versions within the affected range. Version 1.31.9 addresses the NGINX flaws, while the Linux kernel vulnerability requires a separate fix. No active exploitation has been confirmed. Source: https:// nginx2root.com/

Versions 4.0.0 through 6.1.5 are affected, with version 6.1.5 tracked separately as CVE-2026-82384. Apache has released version 6.1.6 to address the vulnerability and urges administrators to upgrade immediately. The attackers' identities and number of compromised servers remain unknown.
